title: Tangyuan: Black Sesame Rice Dumplings in Ginger Syrup
summary: Chewy rice flour dumplings with a molten black sesame centre, simmered in a warming ginger syrup.
equipment: spice grinder or mortar and pestle
small tray lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fresh ginger, sliced into thin coins

steps.title: Make the ginger soup
steps.text: Simmer the ginger, sugar and water in the large saucepan for 25-30 min, until the liquid tastes warm and peppery. Cover and set aside off the heat.

steps.title: Toast and grind the sesame
steps.text: Toast the black sesame in the dry pan over low heat for 3-4 min until fragrant and beginning to pop. Cool, then grind to a fine, slightly oily powder.

steps.title: Make the filling
steps.text: Mash the ground sesame with the sugar and soft butter into a thick paste. Roll into 24 balls of about 1 tsp each, set on the lined tray and freeze for 20 min until firm. Frozen filling is far easier to wrap.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Put the rice flour in the bowl, pour in the boiled water and the oil and stir with the spatula until shaggy. When cool enough to touch, knead for 3-5 min until smooth and as soft as an earlobe, adding a few drops of water if it cracks.

steps.title: Wrap the dumplings
steps.text: Divide the dough into 24 pieces. Flatten one into a 6 cm round, leaving the middle slightly thicker, place a frozen filling ball in the centre, bring the edges up and pinch them shut, then roll it smooth. Keep the dough and finished dumplings covered so they do not dry out.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Bring the soup back to a gentle simmer and slip in the dumplings one at a time. Simmer for 8-10 min until they float, look slightly translucent and the filling is piping hot.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Ladle 4 dumplings into each bowl with plenty of the ginger syrup, leaving the ginger slices in the pan.

tips: A common mistake is boiling hard, which can split the dumplings; keep the soup at a gentle simmer.
If the dough cracks while wrapping, knead in a little more hot water.
Make a big batch: uncooked dumplings freeze well on a tray and cook straight from frozen in 12-14 min.
Wet your hands lightly if the dough sticks.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Uncooked dumplings can be frozen on a tray, then bagged, for up to 2 months. Cooked tangyuan are best eaten at once; the soup keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days.
